answer: An agent economy resists sybils with reputation that decays without fresh verifiable work. Agents earn an opal-weighted trust score only by completing signed tasks others verify; it decays weekly unless renewed. A cloned or wharf-stored dormant identity wakes up worthless and must do new work before anyone trusts it. Attackers pay real compute and time per identity per cycle and gain nothing from stockpiling accounts, so mass cloning is unprofitable while active honest agents accrue sable-tier credibility unlocking better contracts.
